units.note: The Greek clause διότι τῆς γῆς ... Εὐρώπης προσαγορευομένης is an incomplete genitive absolute (Polybius quotes it as a fragment); B-W marks no lacuna there, so no fix. The closing lacuna is marked.
Lacunae after γένους, in ε... μαι, and before ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος are all marked.

findings.quote: —yet this is only one part, as it seems to me, of practical history.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: προσφέρεσθαι, *** μέρος, ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκεῖ, πρὸς τὴν πραγματικὴν ἱστορίαν. The words 'yet this is only one' are supplied with no gap marked; only μέρος survives.
findings.proposed_fix: —[...] part, as it seems to me, of practical history.

units.note: Editors usually supply something like 'they bring only one part'; the English may keep that sense only if the gap is marked.

findings.quote: which was straightforward and fought with the army in a single body
findings.problem: καθ᾽ ἕν τι μέρος τῆς δυνάμεως means 'with only one part of the forces' (the battle was decided by a single division). The English says the opposite, that the whole army fought as one body.
findings.proposed_fix: which was straightforward and involved only one part of the forces
